Hey do we have words for the levels of care we give our dependants?

I both work as a professional caregiver and I take care of my disabled husband.

When I talk here I'd like people to know what I mean when I say things. 

At work we have two different kinds of care companionate, and hands on.

Companionate care is taking care of the house and driving them places but not touching them. So no baths no transfers no doing thier hair etc. 

Hands on care can either be ONLY hands on and no housekeeping or driving but most of the time it's everything. So both companionate and hands on together.

Does this community have any other words for what level of care they give to thier dependants? 

I think having a agreed upon vocabulary would help us understand what we all mean by things. 

Basically if you have a word that you have a definition for list it in the comments so we can all know them.

Why are people so dense to say "if you give me a list, I'll go to the store for you" or "Why don't you do pickup/delivery?" Like I'm not entitled to leave the house or I'm the bedridden person. 

Just give me 2 hours so I can go to the grocery store and feel like a normal person.

From here on when someone asks "is there anything I can do" I'm hitting them with this. 2 hours of sick person watching. That's what I need from you.

Anyone else experience unearned distrust from your loved one?

Guys, this caregiver stuff is so freaking hard. My dad has been a widower since my mom passed in 2013. It’s been a long 11 years, full of many personality shifts in him, and mental & physical decline. My father needs a lot of help. At the same time, he is codependent along side not being able to accept his limitations, if that makes sense? 

He was born deaf, and premature. He also happens to have a low IQ, & was partially raised by foster families during the school year so he could go to deaf school. I feel his circumstances gave him no adult coping skills, no common sense, and possibly contributed to some childhood trauma. He was a great dad for the most part. He seemed more with it & intelligent in my memories of him. When I was about 15, I got emancipated. Long story short, I’m still unpacking my shit from his choices & mistakes from my upbringing. He’s a difficult man to care for, when our history is painful.

He had a difficult knee replacement, and lived in a hospital for 90 days in a neighboring town due to a terrible infection. This is the start of him sabotaging his own wellbeing and health. I stepped up. He moved into my home. It’s crowded, but manageable. But my family didn’t ask to be a part of this. I feel obligated, but in turn they have to shoulder the obligation without getting to choose. My kids & husband have been wonderful. My dad has had around 10 back surgeries total, & something like 32 surgeries in his lifetime. He played football hard in his younger years. He worked physical labor, & with his boomer mentality, working until you are in pain, and then working past that, is normal. His body is tense, solid condensed compacted muscle, fused bones, scar tissue, among other things. 

He has been forgetting he’s paid bills, & paid over, putting himself in the hole. He won’t stop buying off of Facebook, believing scam texts, going down YouTube rabbit holes & believing it all. He ours blind trust into friends who have been shitty to him. My husband & I helped him get a home equity to consolidate debt & get back on his feet. After he was maxed out, but in a better position, He went out & took out a WellsFargo loan & bought a car that he couldn’t afford that lost $25k value the day he drove it home. 

He can’t turn his neck, making driving unsafe. 
I’ve been driving that ridiculous car he’s stuck with. But lately he’s been saying he’s going to take his car, & he’s going to drive it without permission. He said he refuses to believe his body gave up on him. He falls & hurts himself by doing stupid things he knows better than doing.  He had been helping with household bills etc. We would just have him pick up our Sam’s orders, and we paid all the other bills. Everytime we would go over the purchase, and he would comprehend. 2 months later, he’s forgotten, and questioning his bank statement thinking I’ve just taken his card & stolen from him! Then he tells his friends he can’t drive his own car he paid for because his daughter is a bitch. He told my brother that my husband & I are stealing from him & he wants to move. (Absolutely no theft going on here). 

He says crazy off the wall stuff, and I am having a hard time forgiving his blatant distrust of me. My brother refuses to help or even visit. My dad spends all of his time in my home, with his grandkids. He doesn’t have to cook, clean, do laundry, take himself to appointments, feed his dog, among just a few things that we do for him. My dad has a brother who doesn’t care about my dad, screwed him in my grandparents estate, & my dad still trusts him more than I. He’s a narcissist, but also such a basic human. He throws fits like a teen & uses the DARVO method. Such as making statements like “I wish I could be in heaven with my wife,” “I’m just deaf and dumb dad”, or “people know I been like this forever, I never change.” I have to remind him that his wife, is my mom. I lost her too. Why does he blindly trust people who let him down, but distrust & tear down me & my family who care for him the most? Anyone else experience this with their parent? 

TL/DR
Deaf, disabled, dumb dad is ungrateful, trusts strangers, but distrusts me, his only caregiver & family member that talks to him.

Memory care resident sent to ER alone?

Dad fell today and hit his head. Sounds like it is protocol that if they hit their head, EMS must be called. We were told that dad would be taken to the ER with no one accompanying him - that he would be sent with a piece of paper stating that he was a memory care/dementia patient and should not be left alone. I understand that he likely would be seen more quickly as he was arriving by stretcher, but he would not have anyone from the facility with him. (My mom could not go as she is in a wheelchair and very frail). 

Is this normal?! I cannot imagine this going well - he would be confused and agitated, and he hates doctors/hospitals as well. If he was seriously injured we would both jump in our cars to get to him, but that would be at the very least a 3 hour delay. 

How have other folks who have parents far way dealt with this? Thank you so much in advance.

Social Media and Elderly Parent

This might not be the right sub, but I’m not sure where else to post this. If anyone thinks there’s a better place, please let me know’ 


I’m the primary caretaker for my both my elderly parents. My mom is almost completely independent but needs help with technology and paying bills. My sweet, elderly dad recently had a stroke and has Parkinson’s dementia. His cognitive function is basic at best (can’t read, can’t come up with words, can’t process how to work things like microwaves). Recently his Facebook and email got hacked because of links he clicked on. He constantly accidentally posts photos from inside his pocket or his face on Instagram because he doesn’t know how to turn it off.


One of the things he actually still enjoys is scrolling through Instagram reels. That being said he can’t differentiate between reels and ads and he will watch every video all the way through not realizing it’s repeating. Often Instagram will feed him (young) women dancing or doing activities barely dressed. That’s fine and dandy if he wanted to watch those but he doesn’t. He keeps asking why they show up and asking why they don’t go away. He was always a pretty conservative person (didn’t want sex scenes or cursing in movies and TV shows), so I genuinely believe they make him uncomfortable. He wants to see clips of the Beatles, classical music, dogs, babies, and travel videos of Europe.

I keep hitting “not interested” and “don’t show me posts like this” or “this made me uncomfortable” yet they continue to pop up. I don’t want to “take away” this entertainment, but this is a consistent issue. 

Anyone have any ideas how to “safe” mood his videos or content? Any advice in general would be helpful or if you have a better sub to post this in!

TLDR: how to a prevent inappropriate content from appearing on my dads social media.

Has anyone had any success with a therapist who specializes in aging?

My mom is so deeply depressed. She lives in a combination independent and assisted living facility in the assisted wing. She's on the younger side (76) but is there because of a knee injury she was not able to recover from. She can walk a tiny bit with a walker but is basically wheelchair-bound now due to osteoarthritis in her knees. She has not made any friends and has barely met other residents outside of the people they seat her with during meals, which tend to be older and have more cognitive decline than she does. The place also doesn't really seem to have anyone who's job it is to check on your mental/emotional health or try to introduce you to people/get you out of your room. She just spends all day sitting around and watching TV and is so miserable. She was depressed before coming to this place, but has always refused to see a therapist, claiming she did so earlier in her life and never liked it. 

Here's my question: Does anyone have any experience getting their parent to see a therapist who specializes in aging? Was it helpful? I wonder if we could convince her to see someone together with us, under the guise of "family therapy" but then have it really be about helping her and having her establish a relationship with a therapist. 

Any thoughts or anecdotes related to this would be much appreciated!

Childcare and Eldercare are not the same at all

How many times have we heard that our parents took care of us and we owe it to take care of them.  Whereas it is our duty to make sure they are taken care in their old age (although they should be responsible enough to prepare if they can),  it is nothing like taking care of a baby or toddler.  

Babies grow and develop life skills such as walking, eating on their own, using the toilet , dresses themselves, etc.  In a few years , they start school, make friends and become a little less dependent on their parents (they learn to play with others and entertain themselves.    Parents are also most likely a lot younger and have more energy when they have children than when they become caregivers.  You don't see very many 60 year old mothers with small children. 

Elderly parents with dementia are going to the opposite direction.  The become less social and need more and more help.    You either can't go anywhere or you have to hire a caregiver to watch them, with a baby, you can hire a teenager you know. More people are willing to take care of a cute baby than a 100 plus pound dementia person that is often resistant and difficult.  Changing a baby diaper is nothing compared to trying to change an adult.    

And most important, when a baby or toddler falls down, they might cry but they will get up and continue walking. When and old person falls, the break a bone, end up in the hospital and require more care.      Whereas we need to make sure our elderly parents are taken care , comparing it to them taking care us as babies (they brought us into the world, we didn't bring them into the world)  is very wrong.

Struggling being a wife and caregiver

Hi everyone,

I'm 27F and I take care of my disabled husband 46M. He has a genetic kidney disease and is in late stage renal failure, on top of other conditions that make it hard for him to move or do some things on his own. He used to be a business owner but his condition got worse and he retired/sold the business. I've been taking care of him since we've been together (over 2 years now) and I'm just feeling really alone and burnt out. We can never go grocery shopping or on a date without him being in pain in some type of way and he has to sit in the car. We don't have sex due to his health issues/his weight, due to that we opened our marriage. I like meeting new people and getting my needs met but I feel horrible just leaving him at home. He doesn't do anything at all except lay in bed, watches TV, and goes to dialysis. I'm a homebody as well but I would love to be able to do more with him. I'm also autistic/Bipolar so I'm also dealing with my own stuff while making sure he's fine. The house, our pets, our finances, everything falls on me and it's just a lot. I'm so in love with him and always put him before me, but I'm tired of feeling like I'm all alone in my marriage. Do any other wives feel this way or am I being a jerk? 😞

Parents' health and financial crisis

My mom, who isn't very old (63), got very sick last summer. The diagnosis has changed here and there, but the general consensus seems to be that she suffers from viral encephalitis. She lost her job the previous fall, so she was unemployed when she got sick. Now, she's completely incontinent, unable to walk, and has bouts of confusion and irritation. She's currently back at the ER after the physical therapist at the rehab facility she was in found her very confused and with a high fever. 

My father (78; yes, there's a bit of an age gap there) is not doing too well either. He's got neuropathy in both of his legs, and has to get around using a cane with some difficulty (and a lot of pain). He struggles to visit my mom when she's in and out of the hospital. He's actually had a couple of falls in the past month that have required trips to the ER.  It was crazy to me that the rehab facility my mom was in was planning to discharge her this week! My dad would be required to insert a catheter in her every four hours, and help her get around the house. Since he can hardly get around the house himself, it's clear that at least one of them would just end up back in the hospital.

To boot, my mom was the primary money-maker in the family, so her unemployment hit them pretty hard. They accrued a lot of credit card debt. In addition, my mom always handled the financial issues. I think the issues became a lot worse when she got sick and the responsibility fell onto my dad. He recently filed for chapter 13 bankruptcy, but is now struggling to pay the medical bills that they've accrued since. He's on Medicare, but my mom is on what can only be described as the worst health insurance plan that (I believe) they found through Obamacare?

I'm a 26 year old woman, now living in a different part of the country, pursuing my PhD. I was really excited to continue my studies, but now I'm considering taking time off to move in and help my  parents. If I had the money to send them (and I've lent them money here and there to help with bills and such), I would. But the meager graduate student money that I make is definitely not enough. I have one older sibling but he's been pretty useless and unresponsive during this whole situation.

I guess I just don't know what to do. Every day presents new challenges for them. I'm especially close with my mom, so that makes it really difficult for me to be so far away and to see her go through this. I guess I'm looking for advice, but most of all I think I just needed to get this off my chest.

Mom avoidant on final arrangements

Hoping someone could share their experiences with this. My mom had an extended hospitalization about 2 years ago, spent about 6 months in skilled nursing, and is now finally home with a full-time caregiver.

She has been very diligent about her financial matters and keeping her trust up-to-date. She’s financially comfortable, and has a long-term care policy that covers most of her at-home care.

However, she’s been very avoidant about talking about her final wishes (i.e. remains/burial.) I almost feel she has a superstition that if she discusses it or names it, it will hasten in. My late father was not like this at all. In his final years, he was very matter-of-fact about his final wishes, and had everything pre-arranged.

I have gone so far as to offer to take care of my own final arrangements/planning with her, if that would ease her mind. It doesn’t seem to have made a difference. Any experiences or approaches that were successful in breaking through, and having a productive conversation/resolution on this, I’d be interested in hearing.

Ambiguous grief is kicking my butt...

I really could use someone to talk to who understands. 

My fiancé had a brain injury and bilateral stroke 10 months ago. I kind of naturally stepped in to being his caregiver, which now that he is out of rehab I am his 24/7 care while we get set up for services. 

I am thankful for him every day, I love him for who he is now and not just for who he was when we met. But I can't get over this feeling that I will never get to be with the version of himself that he was before the accident ever again. He has speech issues now, and aphasia, and so he can't really talk to me and he has SEVERE short term memory loss. He listens to me when I talk to him and I know he is trying his best every day for me. He is so so patient with me. But I just miss the "old" him so so badly. I miss so many little things about how our life used to be. I feel like I am grieving someone who is still alive, but will never be the same. I have dreams where he is his old self and wake up sobbing. 

It's really emotionally challenging for me to be around him providing care when I am grieving so hard. It's like every little thing stabs into me the knowledge that I will never get that back. I wish I could talk about how hard it is with people without them assuming I am looking for a way out. I still want to spend the rest of my life with this man more than anything else. 

Respite is not an option for at least 2 more weeks while we are getting him set up with a program of services, so I really could use some advice or comfort to help me get through this until then. I feel like I was so overwhelmed trying to adjust and navigate the medical system and help him that I pushed the grief down and now that our lives have slowed down I can't help it. 

The only thought giving me comfort is that this accident didn't just change him, it changed me too. I can't go back to who I was after everything I witnessed either.

87/83 year old parents plan to drive 2 hours to the beach
